quick_skim.title: Which Policy Works, and Where? Estimation and Inference for State-Level Treatment Effects in Difference-in-Differences
quick_skim.abstract: Policies with a common objective and implementation date may differ in details or context. We distinguish the aggregate average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) from sub-aggregate ATTs defined by implementation cohort, jurisdiction, period, or policy type. UN-DID and DID-INT, two DiD estimators that construct jurisdiction-by-time effects, estimate these ATTs under parallel-trends conditions matched to the aggregation. In CPS placebo-law simulations, randomization inference is generally well-sized, though some jurisdiction-specific tests are conservative. The jackknife can be undefined for sub-aggregate ATTs; when defined, it over-rejects with few treated or comparison jurisdictions. Estimands and inference methods should match the policy question and implementation setting.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: Provides DiD estimators for state-level and jurisdiction-specific policy treatment effects, directly applicable to evaluating fiscal and budget program performance.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_cn: 提供州级与辖区层面政策处理效应的双重差分估计方法，可用于评估财政与预算项目绩效。

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Policies with a common objective may have heterogeneous effects across jurisdictions. This paper proposes UN-DID and DID-INT estimators to decompose overall average treatment effects into state-level and sub-aggregate effects under parallel trends, offering inference guidance from CPS placebo-law simulations.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 许多政策在共同目标与实施日期下，其效果可能因辖区而异。现有双重差分方法通常只估计总体平均处理效应，难以回答哪项政策在哪里有效。本文提出UN-DID与DID-INT两种估计量，将总效应分解为州级、辖区、时期等子效应，并给出随机化推断与刀切法的性质。基于CPS安慰剂法模拟，方法在多数情况下具有良好的检验水平，能够支持政府对财政与预算干预效果的精准评价。
